questions.question: How is the Hardy space HpL(Rd) initially defined in the paper?

options.A: As the completion of L² functions whose Hermite heat-semigroup maximal function MLf lies in Lp
options.B: As all distributions with finite Lusin square function only
options.C: As the completion of compactly supported smooth functions under an L² norm
options.D: As functions whose Hermite Riesz transforms are integrable

questions.rationale: The definition uses MLf(x)=supt>0|e−tLf(x)| and the Lp quasi-norm.
questions.evidence_quote: We deﬁne HpL(Rd) as the completion

questions.question: Which derivative vector appears in the Lusin integral associated with the Hermite operator?
questions.rationale: The area function uses the Hermite-specific creation-type derivatives ∂j+xj.

questions.question: What is the domain of integration in the Lusin area function Sf(x)?

options.A: The cone Γ(x)={(y,t):|x−y|<t} with measure t^(1−d)dy dt
options.C: All y∈Rd at a single scale t

questions.rationale: The area function integrates the squared gradient of the Poisson semigroup over this cone.

questions.question: For which dimension and p range is the main Hardy-space characterization stated?
questions.rationale: The abstract and theorem assumptions use d∈{3,4,…} and p∈(0,1].

questions.question: What equivalence is established by Theorem 1.1?

options.A: HpL and HpS coincide as quasi-normed spaces
options.B: HpL equals the L² Sobolev space
options.C: The maximal space equals only the atomic space for p=1
options.D: HpS embeds strictly into HpL for all p

questions.rationale: Theorem 1.1 identifies the heat-maximal Hardy space with the Lusin-integral space.

questions.question: Under what radius condition must an HpL atom satisfy the cancellation moment condition ∫a=0?

options.B: For every ball regardless of radius

questions.rationale: Definition 2.4 imposes cancellation only for sufficiently small balls relative to ρ(x0).

questions.question: How does the paper define the local scale function ρ(x)?
questions.rationale: The preliminary section sets the scale function explicitly.

questions.question: What is the bounded operator in Theorem 1.2, and on which spaces is it asserted bounded?

options.A: RLj=(∂j+xj)L^(−1/2) is bounded on HpL for every j
options.B: L itself is bounded on HpS for j=1 only
options.C: The Poisson semigroup is bounded on Lp for p>1
options.D: RLj=(∂j−xj)L is bounded only for p=1

questions.rationale: Theorem 1.2 gives boundedness of the Hermite Riesz transforms for all coordinate indices.
questions.evidence_quote: The operators RLj is bounded on HpL(Rd) for all j

questions.question: What intermediate atomic decomposition range is used in Proposition 2.5?

options.A: d/(d+δ)<p≤1, where δ is the regularity exponent from the kernel estimate

questions.rationale: The atomic result is stated for p above the dimension-dependent threshold involving δ.
questions.evidence_quote: d d+δ < p ≤ 1, where δ is given by (3).

questions.question: What operator comparison is used to place HpL inside HpL+2 in the Riesz-transform proof?

options.A: ML+2f≤MLf pointwise because of the factor e^(−2t)
options.B: MLf≤ML+2f because adding 2 increases the semigroup
options.C: The two maximal operators differ by a constant independent of f
options.D: The proof uses equality of the generators L and L+2

questions.rationale: Since e−(L+2)t=e−2t e−tL and e−2t≤1, the shifted maximal function is dominated.
